item.title: Pakistan Says Deal Is Close Even as Iran, US Harden Stances
item.content:encoded: Pakistan’s defense minister said the US and Iran are “close to some sort of arrangement” over the Strait of Hormuz, even after both sides appeared to toughen their positions in the long-deadlocked negotiations. Noam Raydan, William Sudhaus Senior Fellow at The Near East Institute says the data shows that the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea will remain essential choke points. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fmr. FDA, CDC Official on Cyclospora, Food Safety Issues
item.content:encoded: Steve Ostroff, Former Acting Commissioner of the FDA and Former Deputy Director of the National Center for Infectious Diseases at the CDC, joined the program to discuss the public awareness timeline of the cyclospora outbreak. The conversation highlighted that while the outbreak became widely known in early to mid-July, there were reports suggesting that government agencies had knowledge of the issue weeks prior to public disclosure. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Deep Dive Into The US' Critical Minerals Investment
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Senior Economic Statecraft Reporter Joe Deaux joins Tim Stenovec and Kristine Aquino for a one-hour special of Businessweek Daily to answer all your questions about rare earths and the $3 Billion US investment in the critical minerals industry. Investigative Reporter Polly Mosendz discusses her report on how "Trump Is Rewriting Corporate Norms With 211-Mile Arctic Road." Plus, Gracelin Baskaran -- Director of Critical Minerals Security Program at CSIS -- breaks down the global viability of the rare earths trade. Then, Quince Street Strategy Principal Tripp Hornick talks about the domestic-side of the investment, and what it means for companies trying take advantage in a growing industry. (Source: Bloomberg)
